56481.q: Which capital lies in the Blue Banana?
56481.e: The Blue Banana reaches from England via the Benelux countries and the Rhine area to northern Italy. Brussels lies right in the middle.
56481.m: Brussels lies in the Blue Banana.

56482.q: Which river forms an important transport route in the Blue Banana?
56482.e: Many industrial areas and cities lie along the Rhine, such as Basel, Cologne and the Ruhr. The Rhine is one of the busiest waterways in the world.
56482.m: The Rhine is the lifeline of the Blue Banana.

56483.q: Which Swiss city with an important Rhine port lies in the Blue Banana?
56483.e: Basel lies on the Rhine and has the Swiss Rhine Ports. From here ships can travel all the way to the North Sea.
56483.m: Basel is Switzerland’s gateway to the Rhine.

56484.q: Where does the “Blue Banana” get its name from?
a: From its curved shape on the map
From banana imports in the ports
56484.e: On the map the economic region forms a curved strip. The blue colour probably recalls the European flag.
56484.m: The Blue Banana is named after its shape on the map.

56485.q: Which Italian economic metropolis lies at the southern end of the Blue Banana?
56485.e: Milan is the industrial and financial centre of northern Italy. The Blue Banana ends in the south with the area around Milan.
56485.m: Milan forms the southern end of the Blue Banana.

56486.q: Which German industrial region lies in the Blue Banana?
56486.e: The Ruhr is one of the largest urban areas in Europe and lies close to the Rhine. In the past, coal and steel shaped the region.
56486.m: The Ruhr is part of the Blue Banana.

56487.q: Which is the largest seaport in Europe?
56487.e: More than 400 million tonnes of goods are handled in the port of Rotterdam every year. No other port in Europe reaches this amount.
56487.m: Rotterdam is the largest port in Europe.

56488.q: At the mouth of which rivers does the port of Rotterdam lie?
56488.e: Rotterdam lies in the shared delta of the Rhine and the Meuse. This connects ships directly with the inland regions.
56488.m: Rotterdam lies at the mouth of the Rhine and the Meuse.

56489.q: How did the port of Rotterdam gain new land for port facilities?
a: It pumped sand into the sea
56489.e: For the Maasvlakte 2 area, sand was pumped into the North Sea. This created new land where the largest container ships dock.
56489.m: Rotterdam built up port land in the sea.

56490.q: Why is the port of Rotterdam important for Switzerland?
a: Goods reach Basel by Rhine ship
Trains from there go only to Switzerland
56490.e: Rhine ships bring goods such as containers and fuel from Rotterdam to the Rhine ports of Basel. This gives Switzerland access to the sea.
56490.m: Switzerland is linked to Rotterdam via the Rhine.

56491.q: Rotterdam was the largest port in the world until 2004. On which continent are the ports that have overtaken it since then?
56491.e: Ports such as Shanghai and Singapore grew strongly through world trade. But Rotterdam is still the largest port in Europe.
56491.m: Today the largest ports in the world are in Asia.

56492.q: Which goods are handled in particularly large amounts at the port of Rotterdam and processed in refineries?
56492.e: Rotterdam is a centre of the oil industry with several refineries. Crude oil is one of the port’s most important goods.
56492.m: A great deal of oil is handled in Rotterdam.

56493.q: Which Belgian port is the second largest seaport in Europe after Rotterdam?
56493.e: The port of Antwerp lies on the Scheldt and has been merged with Bruges since 2022. It is the second largest port in Europe.
56493.m: Antwerp is the second largest port in Europe.

56494.q: Into which sea do ships sail from the port of Rotterdam?
56494.e: A dug waterway, the Nieuwe Waterweg, connects Rotterdam directly with the North Sea.
56494.m: Rotterdam is connected to the North Sea.

56495.q: What is France’s high-speed train called?
56495.e: TGV stands for “train à grande vitesse”, meaning high-speed train. In regular service it travels at up to 320 km/h.
56495.m: The TGV is France’s fast train.

56496.q: Which train holds the speed record for wheeled trains on rails?
56496.e: On 3 April 2007 a modified TGV reached 574.8 km/h. This is still the record for wheel-on-rail trains.
56496.m: At almost 575 km/h, the TGV holds the rail record.

56497.q: What are Deutsche Bahn’s high-speed trains called?
56497.e: ICE stands for Intercity-Express. On new lines the trains travel at up to 300 km/h, and they also come to Basel and Zurich.
56497.m: The ICE is Germany’s fast train.

56498.q: Which country in Europe has the longest network of high-speed lines?
56498.e: Since 1992 Spain has built a very large network totalling almost 4,000 kilometres. The lines connect Madrid with many large cities in the country.
56498.m: Spain has the longest high-speed network in Europe.

56499.q: Through which tunnel does the Eurostar travel from London to Paris?
56499.e: The Channel Tunnel is about 50 kilometres long and runs under the English Channel. It connects England with France.
56499.m: The Eurostar travels through the Channel Tunnel.

56500.q: Roughly what is the top speed of high-speed trains such as the TGV or ICE?
56500.e: On new high-speed lines, the TGV and ICE travel at up to about 300 km/h in everyday service, the TGV even up to 320 km/h.
56500.m: Fast trains travel at up to about 300 km/h.

56501.q: Which Italian high-speed train has a name meaning “red arrow”?
56501.e: “Freccia” means arrow and “rossa” means red. The Frecciarossa travels at up to 300 km/h between Italy’s large cities.
56501.m: The Frecciarossa is Italy’s red arrow.

56502.q: Which cities did the first TGV line connect from 1981?
56502.e: The Paris-Lyon line was the first high-speed line in Europe. It greatly reduced the journey time.
56502.m: The first TGV ran from Paris to Lyon.

56503.q: What is the high-speed train that connects Switzerland directly with Paris called?
56503.e: TGV Lyria runs from Zurich, Basel, Geneva and Lausanne, among others, to Paris. From Basel the journey takes only about three hours.
56503.m: You can travel from Switzerland to Paris with the TGV Lyria.

56504.q: About how long is the Gotthard Road Tunnel, opened in 1980?
56504.e: The Gotthard Road Tunnel is 16.9 kilometres long and connects Göschenen with Airolo. A second tube has been under construction since 2021.
56504.m: The Gotthard Road Tunnel is about 17 kilometres long.

56505.q: In which year was the first Gotthard railway tunnel opened?
56505.e: The summit tunnel between Göschenen and Airolo, about 15 kilometres long, opened in 1882. More than 190 workers died during its construction.
56505.m: The Gotthard railway has run through the mountain since 1882.

56506.q: Which NRLA tunnel was the first to open, in 2007?
56506.e: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is about 35 kilometres long. It connects the Bernese Oberland with Valais.
56506.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel went into service in 2007 as the first NRLA tunnel.

56507.q: Which base tunnel in Ticino completed the flat railway route through the Alps in 2020?
56507.e: The Ceneri Base Tunnel is about 15 kilometres long and lies between Bellinzona and Lugano. With it, the Gotthard route is flat all the way through.
56507.m: The Ceneri Base Tunnel opened in 2020.

56508.q: What does the Alpine Initiative, accepted in 1994, call for?
a: Moving freight from road to rail
A ban on all lorries in Switzerland
56508.e: The people accepted the Alpine Initiative in 1994. Freight through the Alps should travel by train rather than by lorry wherever possible.
56508.m: The Alpine Initiative wants to move goods onto the railway.

56509.q: What is the charge that lorries in Switzerland pay according to distance and weight called?
56509.e: The distance-related heavy vehicle fee (HVF) has existed since 2001. Part of the money was used to build the NRLA.
56509.m: The heavy vehicle fee makes lorry journeys more expensive and supports the railway.

56510.q: Which Alpine pass between Austria and Italy is one of the busiest in the Alps?
56510.e: Millions of lorries cross the Brenner every year. A base tunnel for the railway is being built underneath it.
56510.m: The Brenner is Austria’s most important Alpine crossing.

56511.q: What is the transport of whole lorries on goods trains through the Alps called?
56511.e: On the rolling motorway, lorries travel on low-floor railway wagons. The drivers travel along in a separate carriage.
56511.m: On the rolling motorway, lorries travel by train.

56512.q: Which country in the European Union produces the farm products with the greatest value?
56512.e: France has a lot of fertile land and a favourable climate. It produces especially large amounts of grain, milk, meat and wine.
56512.m: France is the largest farming country in the EU.

56513.q: Which small European country is one of the largest exporters of farm products in the world?
56513.e: The Netherlands export a great deal of vegetables, flowers, dairy products and meat. Modern greenhouses make high yields possible.
56513.m: Despite its small size, the Netherlands is a farming giant.

56514.q: Which country is often called the “breadbasket of Europe” because of its fertile black earth soils?
56514.e: Ukraine has wide areas of very fertile black earth. The country exports a lot of wheat, maize and sunflower oil.
56514.m: Ukraine is the breadbasket of Europe.

56515.q: Which country is the largest producer of olive oil in the world?
56515.e: Huge olive groves grow especially in Andalusia. In normal harvest years almost half of the world’s olive oil comes from Spain.
56515.m: Spain produces the most olive oil.

56516.q: What is grown in the “sea of plastic” in southern Spain?
56516.e: In the province of Almería there are huge greenhouses made of plastic sheeting. In winter a lot of vegetables come from there to the rest of Europe.
56516.m: Vegetables for Europe grow in the sea of plastic.

56517.q: What is land in the Netherlands that has been reclaimed from the sea and enclosed by dykes called?
56517.e: Polders often lie below sea level and are protected by dykes. Pumps keep the land dry so that it can be used as fields or pasture.
56517.m: A polder is land reclaimed from the sea.

56518.q: What is the shared policy with which the EU has supported its farming since 1962 called?
56518.e: The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) pays subsidies to farmers and regulates the farm market. It is one of the largest items in the EU budget.
56518.m: With the Common Agricultural Policy, the EU supports its farmers.

56519.q: Which type of farming is most common in the Swiss mountain areas?
56519.e: In the mountains, meadows and pastures are better suited than fields. In summer the cows often graze on the alpine pastures.
56519.m: In the Swiss mountains, farmers mainly keep cows.

56520.q: Which French region does real champagne come from?
56520.e: Only sparkling wine from the Champagne region in north-eastern France may be called champagne. The name is protected.

56521.q: In which country is the Rioja wine region?
56521.e: Rioja lies in northern Spain on the river Ebro. It is known for red wines made from the Tempranillo grape.
56521.m: Rioja is a famous wine region in Spain.

56522.q: Which wine comes from the Douro Valley in Portugal?
56522.e: Port is made in the Douro Valley. It gets its name from the city of Porto, from where it was shipped.
56522.m: Port comes from the Douro Valley.

56523.q: Which wine region on Lake Geneva has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007?
56523.e: The vineyard terraces of Lavaux lie between Lausanne and Montreux. They were built on the steep slopes over centuries.
56523.m: The vineyard terraces of Lavaux are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

56524.q: Which canton has the largest vineyard area in Switzerland?
56524.e: About a third of Switzerland’s vineyard area is in Valais. The sunny, dry climate is ideal for it.
56524.m: Valais is the largest wine canton in Switzerland.

56525.q: What is the harvest of grapes in autumn called?
56525.e: During the grape harvest, the ripe grapes are cut from the vines. In Swiss German it is also called “Wümmet”.
56525.m: Picking the grapes is called the grape harvest.

56526.q: In which country is the famous Tokaj wine region?
56526.e: Tokaj lies in north-eastern Hungary. The sweet Tokaji wines are well known.
56526.m: Tokaji is a wine from Hungary.

56527.q: Along which German river do vines grow on particularly steep slopes?
56527.e: Wine has been grown on the steep slate slopes of the Moselle since Roman times.
56527.m: Vines grow on steep slopes along the Moselle.

56528.q: Which country invests its income from North Sea oil in the largest sovereign wealth fund in the world?
56528.e: Norway saves its oil income in a state fund for future generations. The fund owns shares in thousands of companies around the world.
56528.m: Norway saves its oil money in a huge state fund.

56529.q: From where is oil extracted in the North Sea?
56529.e: The oil lies deep under the seabed. Large drilling rigs, also called oil platforms, have been bringing it up since the end of the 1960s.
56529.m: North Sea oil is extracted with drilling rigs.

56530.q: Which North Sea oil field gave its name to an important benchmark grade for the oil price?
56530.e: The Brent field lies east of the Shetland Islands. The price of “Brent” is an important worldwide benchmark for the oil price.
56530.m: The oil price is often given for Brent crude.

56531.q: In which country is the oil city of Aberdeen?
56531.e: Aberdeen lies on the North Sea coast of Scotland. From there the oil platforms are supplied by helicopters and ships.

56532.q: In which country is the oil city of Stavanger?
56532.e: Stavanger lies on the west coast of Norway. Many oil companies are based there, and there is even an oil museum.

56533.q: What happened on the Piper Alpha oil platform in the North Sea in 1988?
a: An explosion with a huge fire
56533.e: On Piper Alpha off Scotland, gas exploded and a huge fire broke out. 167 people died. Afterwards the safety rules were made stricter.
56533.m: The Piper Alpha disaster led to stricter safety rules.

56534.q: What did the disused oil storage buoy “Brent Spar” become known for in 1995?
a: Protests prevented it being sunk in the sea
It was the first wooden oil tanker
It brought oil all the way to Switzerland
It was the largest drilling rig in the world
56534.e: The company wanted to sink the disused facility in the Atlantic. After protests by Greenpeace and many customers, it was taken apart on land.
56534.m: After protests, Brent Spar was disposed of on land.

56535.q: Why has oil production in the British part of the North Sea been falling since about 2000?
a: The North Sea has become too deep
56535.e: British production reached its peak in 1999. Since then many oil fields have been largely used up.
56535.m: The North Sea oil fields are slowly running out.

56536.q: Which country built the world’s first offshore wind farm in 1991?
56536.e: The Vindeby wind farm with eleven turbines was built off the Danish coast in 1991. It was in operation until 2017.
56536.m: The first wind farm at sea was in Denmark.

56537.q: What is an offshore wind farm?
a: Wind turbines in the sea off the coast
56537.e: “Offshore” means “off the coast”. The wind turbines stand on foundations in the seabed.
56537.m: An offshore wind farm stands in the sea.

56538.q: Why is the North Sea particularly suitable for wind farms?
a: The wind is strong and the sea is shallow
56538.e: Over the sea the wind blows more strongly and steadily than on land. Because the North Sea is shallow in many places, foundations are easy to build.
56538.m: In the North Sea a lot of wind blows over shallow water.

56539.q: What are the wind turbines in an offshore wind farm for?
56539.e: The wind turns the rotors, and a generator in the turbine turns this into electricity. Germany’s first wind farm at sea, alpha ventus, went into operation in 2010.
56539.m: Wind turbines turn wind into electricity.

56540.q: Which country has the largest offshore wind power capacity in Europe (as of 2024)?
56540.e: Some of the largest wind farms in the world, such as Hornsea, stand off the British coast. Germany follows in second place.
56540.m: Great Britain has the most wind power at sea.

56541.q: On which sandbank in the North Sea is a wind farm being built that is set to become the largest in the world?
56541.e: Dogger Bank lies about 130 kilometres off the English coast and is only 15 to 36 metres deep there. The Dogger Bank wind farm is being built in several stages.
56541.m: A huge wind farm is being built on Dogger Bank.

56542.q: How does the electricity from offshore wind farms get to land?
a: Through undersea cables on the seabed
56542.e: The wind turbines are connected to a substation platform. From there, undersea cables carry the electricity to the grid on land.
56542.m: Wind power comes ashore through undersea cables.

56543.q: In which country is the port city of Esbjerg, a centre of wind power?
56543.e: Esbjerg lies on Denmark’s North Sea coast. Many wind turbines for wind farms at sea are shipped from there.
56543.m: Esbjerg is a centre of wind power in Denmark.

56544.q: Which country is the most visited tourist destination in the world?
56544.e: France welcomes about 100 million foreign visitors every year. Paris, the Côte d’Azur and the Alps are popular.
56544.m: France is the most popular tourist destination in the world.

56545.q: Which museum is the most visited art museum in the world?
56545.e: The Louvre in Paris has almost 9 million visitors a year. The Mona Lisa hangs there too.
56545.m: The Louvre in Paris is the most visited museum in the world.

56546.q: Which city has charged day visitors an entry fee on certain days since 2024?
56546.e: Venice is visited by a huge number of day tourists. The fee is meant to manage the crowds and protect the old town.
56546.m: Venice charges day visitors an entry fee.

a: Too many tourists put a strain on a place
56547.e: With overtourism, residents, nature and sights suffer from the crowds. Examples are Venice, Barcelona or Hallstatt.
56547.m: Overtourism means too many tourists overload a place.

56548.q: After France, which country is the second most popular tourist destination in the world?
56548.e: Spain welcomed about 94 million foreign visitors in 2024. The Mediterranean beaches and the islands are especially popular.
56548.m: Spain is one of the most popular tourist destinations in the world.

56549.q: Where is the highest railway station in Europe?
56549.e: Jungfraujoch station lies at 3454 metres above sea level. It is marketed as the “Top of Europe” and attracts visitors from all over the world.
56549.m: Jungfraujoch station is the highest in Europe.

56550.q: Which holiday resort at the foot of the Matterhorn is car-free?
56550.e: In Zermatt, normal cars with combustion engines are not allowed. Visitors arrive by train and get around the village in electric vehicles.
56550.m: Zermatt is a car-free holiday resort.

56551.q: What is the rocky coast between Barcelona and the French border, a popular holiday area, called?
56551.e: Costa Brava means “wild coast”. It lies in Catalonia and is known for its coves.
56551.m: The Costa Brava lies in north-eastern Spain.

56552.q: Which architect designed the Sagrada Família in Barcelona?
56552.e: Antoni Gaudí worked on the church for over 40 years. It is still not finished and is one of the most visited sights in Spain.
56552.m: The Sagrada Família is a work by Gaudí.

56553.q: In which country is the tidal power station on the Rance, opened in 1966?
56553.e: The power station lies in Brittany near Saint-Malo. Until 2011 it was the largest tidal power station in the world.
56553.m: The tidal power station on the Rance is in France.

56554.q: What does a tidal power station use to produce electricity?
a: Ebb and flow of the tides
56554.e: At high tide water flows into a bay, at low tide it flows out again. As it does so, it drives turbines.
56554.m: A tidal power station uses the rise and fall of the tides.

56555.q: What mainly causes the tides, the rise and fall of the sea?
56555.e: The Moon pulls on the water of the oceans and so creates tidal bulges. The Sun also plays a part, but more weakly.
56555.m: The Moon is the main reason for the tides.

56556.q: Why was the tidal power station on the Rance built in Brittany of all places?
a: The tidal range there is very large
The sea is especially warm there
France’s longest river flows into the sea there
56556.e: In the Rance estuary the difference between low and high tide can be more than 12 metres. The larger this tidal range, the more electricity can be produced.
56556.m: Tidal power stations need a large tidal range.

56557.q: Which European country produces about 90 per cent of its electricity from hydropower?
56557.e: Norway has many mountains, lakes and a lot of rain and snow. That is why almost all its electricity comes from hydroelectric power stations.
56557.m: Norway produces almost all its electricity from hydropower.

56558.q: What is the highest gravity dam in the world, in the canton of Valais, called?
56558.e: The Grande Dixence dam is 285 metres high. It holds back the Lac des Dix in the Val d’Hérémence.
56558.m: The Grande Dixence is the highest gravity dam in the world.

56559.q: On which river is the large Iron Gate hydroelectric power station between Serbia and Romania?
56559.e: At the Iron Gate the Danube breaks through the Carpathians. Two large power stations dam the river there.
56559.m: The Iron Gate power station lies on the Danube.

56560.q: In which year did Geneva become part of the Swiss Confederation?
56560.e: After French rule ended, Geneva joined the Confederation as a canton in 1815. The Congress of Vienna confirmed this step.
56560.m: Geneva has been a Swiss canton since 1815.

56561.q: Which reformer worked in Geneva in the 16th century?
56561.e: John Calvin made Geneva a centre of the Reformation. That is why the city was also called the “Protestant Rome”.
56561.m: Calvin shaped the Reformation in Geneva.

56562.q: Who is shown on the big Reformation Wall in Geneva?
56562.e: The Reformation monument in the Parc des Bastions shows large statues of reformers, including John Calvin.
56562.m: The Reformation Wall in Geneva shows the reformers.

56563.q: What is the cathedral in Geneva's old town called?
56563.e: A famous reformer preached in St Pierre Cathedral in the 16th century. From the north tower you can see over the whole city.

56564.q: Which United Nations organisation for health has its headquarters in Geneva?
56564.e: The World Health Organization (WHO) was founded in 1948. It deals with health issues all over the world, for example vaccination programmes.
56564.m: The WHO has its headquarters in Geneva.

56565.q: Which famous philosopher was born in Geneva in 1712?
56565.e: Rousseau wrote important works about education and the state. There is a statue of him on Rousseau Island in Geneva.

56566.q: Which international agreements to protect the wounded and prisoners in war are named after Geneva?
56566.e: The first Geneva Convention was signed in Geneva in 1864. Today almost every country in the world has accepted the agreements of 1949.
56566.m: The Geneva Conventions protect people in war.

56567.q: Which canton ruled Vaud as a subject territory until 1798?
56567.e: Bern conquered Vaud in 1536 and ruled it for over 250 years through bailiffs. Only in 1798 did Vaud free itself.
56567.m: For a long time Vaud was a subject territory of Bern.

56568.q: In which town in Vaud does the Fête des Vignerons take place?
56568.e: The great winegrowers' festival only takes place about every 20 to 25 years, most recently in 2019. It is a UNESCO living cultural heritage.
56568.m: The Fête des Vignerons is celebrated in Vevey.

56569.q: Which canton in western Switzerland has the most inhabitants?
56569.e: Vaud has over 800,000 inhabitants and, after Zurich and Bern, is the third-largest canton by population (as of 2024).
56569.m: Vaud is the most populous canton in French-speaking Switzerland.

56570.q: Which man from Vaud was executed in 1723 because he wanted to free Vaud from Bernese rule?
56570.e: Jean Daniel Abraham Davel marched to Lausanne with soldiers in 1723, but found no support. Today he is seen as a folk hero of Vaud.
56570.m: Major Davel is a hero of Vaud.

56571.q: Which European football association has its headquarters in Nyon?
56571.e: UEFA is Europe's football association and organises, for example, the Champions League and the European Championship. Its headquarters are on Lake Geneva in Nyon.
56571.m: UEFA has its headquarters in Nyon.

56572.q: What is the big open-air festival that takes place near Nyon every summer called?
56572.e: The Paléo Festival has been held since 1976 and is one of the biggest open-air festivals in Switzerland. It lasts six days.
56572.m: The Paléo Festival takes place near Nyon.

56573.q: Which famous film comedian spent the last 25 years of his life near Vevey?
56573.e: He lived from early 1953 until his death in 1977 at the Manoir de Ban in Corsier-sur-Vevey. Today there is a museum there about his life and his films.
56573.m: Charlie Chaplin lived on Lake Geneva near Vevey.

56574.q: Which flower festival takes place every spring in Morges on Lake Geneva?
56574.e: In the Parc de l'Indépendance over 100,000 tulips bloom in April and May. The festival is called the Fête de la Tulipe.
56574.m: Every spring Morges celebrates the tulip festival.

56575.q: What is the Gothic cathedral of Lausanne called?
56575.e: Notre-Dame Cathedral was consecrated in the 13th century. It is seen as one of the most beautiful Gothic buildings in Switzerland.

56576.q: Which big international sports organisation has its headquarters in Lausanne?
56576.e: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) is based in Lausanne. That is why Lausanne calls itself the Olympic Capital. FIFA is based in Zurich, UEFA in Nyon.

56577.q: Which form of transport is found in Switzerland only in Lausanne?
56577.e: Lausanne is the only Swiss city with a metro. Line M2 climbs over 300 metres from the lake to the upper town.
56577.m: Lausanne has the only metro in Switzerland.

56578.q: Who founded a settlement on the lakeshore of today's Lausanne about 2000 years ago?
56578.e: The Romans called their settlement Lousonna. It was near today's district of Vidy, where you can still see ruins and a museum.
56578.m: The Romans already settled in Lausanne.

56579.q: Which Olympic Games took place in Lausanne in January 2020?
56579.e: Young athletes aged 15 to 18 took part in these Games. Some events also took place elsewhere in Vaud, in Valais, in the Grisons and in France.
56579.m: Lausanne hosted the Winter Youth Olympic Games in 2020.

56580.q: On which lake does the city of Lausanne lie?
56580.e: Lausanne lies on the northern shore of Lake Geneva, which is called Lac Léman in French. The city climbs steeply up the slope from the shore.

56581.q: What was found at La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel?
a: Weapons and tools of the Celts
56581.e: Many Celtic swords, jewellery and tools came to light at La Tène. A period of the Iron Age is named after the site.
56581.m: Many Celtic objects were found at La Tène.

56582.q: What is the big waterfall on the Doubs near Les Brenets called?
56582.e: There the Doubs plunges about 27 metres. The waterfall lies on the border with France.
56582.m: The Saut du Doubs is a waterfall on the border with France.

56583.q: On which day does the canton of Neuchâtel celebrate the founding of its republic every year?
56583.e: On 1 March 1848 republicans marched to Neuchâtel and removed the royal government. This day is a public holiday in the canton.
56583.m: 1 March is the holiday of the Republic of Neuchâtel.

56584.q: Which big museum about timekeeping is in La Chaux-de-Fonds?
56584.e: The Musée international d'horlogerie shows thousands of clocks, watches and instruments from many centuries. Part of it is underground.
56584.m: There is a big watch and clock museum in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

56585.q: In which building do the government and parliament of the canton of Neuchâtel meet?
a: In the town hall of Le Locle
56585.e: The castle stands on a hill above the old town, right next to the Collegiate Church. It has been the seat of the cantonal authorities for centuries.
56585.m: The Neuchâtel government works in the castle.

56586.q: Which raw material was mined in the Val-de-Travers until 1986?
56586.e: In the La Presta mines, rock containing asphalt was dug out for road surfaces. Today you can visit the tunnels.
56586.m: Asphalt used to be mined in the Val-de-Travers.

56587.q: What special thing can you see at the Col-des-Roches in Le Locle?
56587.e: The underground mills used the power of a stream that disappears into a cave. They have been restored and are now a museum.
56587.m: In Le Locle mills used to turn underground.

56588.q: What is the region around Porrentruy in the north of the canton of Jura called?
56588.e: The Ajoie sticks out into France like a nose. Its main town is Porrentruy (Pruntrut in German).
56588.m: The Ajoie is the northernmost region of the Jura.

56589.q: Which canton did the Jura separate from when it became a canton of its own in 1979?
56589.e: The northern Jura belonged to the canton of Bern until 1978. After several popular votes it became a canton of its own in 1979.
56589.m: The canton of Jura used to be part of the canton of Bern.

56591.q: What was discovered when the A16 motorway was built near Porrentruy?
56591.e: During construction thousands of dinosaur footprints from the Jurassic came to light. Today they are on show in the Jurassica museum.
56591.m: Thousands of dinosaur tracks were found near Porrentruy.

56593.q: What is the A16 motorway, which runs through the Jura from Biel to Boncourt, called?
56593.e: The Transjurane connects the Jura with the Swiss Plateau and France. It has many tunnels and bridges.
56593.m: The A16 motorway is called the Transjurane.

56594.q: The German name of this town is Delsberg. What is it called in French?
56594.e: French is spoken in the canton of Jura, so Delémont is the official name. “Delsberg” is the German name.
56594.m: Delsberg is called Delémont in French.

56595.q: Delémont is the capital of which canton?
56595.e: Delémont, Delsberg in German, is the capital of the canton of Jura.
56595.m: Delémont is the capital of the canton of Jura.

56596.q: Roughly how many inhabitants does Delémont have (as of 2023)?
56596.e: At the end of 2023, 12,739 people lived in Delémont. Even so, it is the biggest municipality in the canton of Jura.
56596.m: Delémont is a small capital with about 12,700 inhabitants.

56597.q: What is special about the canton of Jura, whose capital is Delémont?
56597.e: The canton of Jura separated from the canton of Bern and has existed since 1979. This makes it the youngest canton in Switzerland.
56597.m: The Jura is the youngest canton in Switzerland.

56598.q: In which year did Fribourg join the Swiss Confederation?
56598.e: Fribourg was admitted in 1481 together with Solothurn. The Agreement of Stans made this possible.
56598.m: Fribourg has been part of the Confederation since 1481.

56599.q: To which saint is the cathedral of Fribourg dedicated?
56599.e: The Gothic Cathedral of St Nicholas is the landmark of the city of Fribourg. Its tower is about 74 metres high.
56599.m: Fribourg's cathedral is called St Nicholas.

56600.q: Which Swiss university calls itself the only bilingual university in the country?
56600.e: At the University of Fribourg you can study in German and French. It was founded in 1889.
56600.m: In Fribourg you study in German and French.

56601.q: Which district of Fribourg is mainly German-speaking?
56601.e: The Sense district lies in the east of the canton on the border with Bern. People there speak the Sensler German dialect.
56601.m: German is spoken in the Sense district.

56603.q: Which town is the second biggest in the canton of Fribourg after the capital?
56603.e: Bulle is the main town of the Gruyère district and has been growing fast for years. The town has over 20,000 inhabitants.
56603.m: Bulle is the second biggest town in the canton of Fribourg.

56604.q: What is the traditional harvest festival with a big feast in the canton of Fribourg called?
56604.e: The Bénichon (Kilbi in German) includes a long menu with cakes, meat and saffron bread. It is celebrated in autumn, when the cows come back from the alpine pastures.
56604.m: In autumn the people of Fribourg celebrate the Bénichon.

56605.q: Which noble family founded the town of Fribourg in 1157?
56605.e: Duke Berchtold IV of Zähringen founded the town on a loop of the Saane. The Zähringer also founded other towns such as Bern.
56605.m: Fribourg was founded by the Zähringer.

56606.q: Which spa resort in Valais is known for its hot thermal springs?
56606.e: A great deal of warm water flows out of the springs of Leukerbad every day. Guests came to bathe there as early as the Middle Ages.
56606.m: In Leukerbad you bathe in warm thermal water.

56607.q: In which valley in Valais do the Tschäggättä roam around with wooden masks at carnival time?
56607.e: The Tschäggättä wear carved wooden masks and sheepskins. The custom is very old in the Lötschental.
56607.m: The Tschäggättä belong to the Lötschental.

56608.q: Which Roman building can you still see in Martigny today?
56608.e: The Romans built an amphitheatre in Martigny for games and fights. Today, for example, cow fights take place there.
56608.m: There is a Roman amphitheatre in Martigny.

56609.q: Which monastery in Valais has existed without interruption since the year 515?
56609.e: The Abbey of Saint-Maurice is seen as the oldest continuously existing monastery in the Western world. Its church treasure is very valuable.
56609.m: The Abbey of Saint-Maurice is over 1500 years old.

56610.q: By area, where does Valais rank among the biggest cantons in Switzerland?
56610.e: Valais covers about 5200 square kilometres. Only the Grisons and Bern are bigger.
56610.m: Valais is the third biggest canton in Switzerland.

56611.q: Roughly how high above sea level is the town of Sion?
56611.e: The old town of Sion lies in the Rhône valley at about 500 metres above sea level. But the mountains all around are over 3000 metres high.
56611.m: Sion lies about 500 metres above sea level.

56612.q: What are the two castle hills rising above Sion called?
56612.e: On Valère stands a fortified church, on Tourbillon a castle ruin. The two hills are the landmark of Sion.
56612.m: Valère and Tourbillon are the castle hills of Sion.

56613.q: What is in the basilica on Valère hill in Sion?
a: One of the oldest playable organs in the world
The longest wooden bridge in Switzerland
56613.e: The organ of the Valère Basilica dates from around 1430. It is still played at concerts today.
56613.m: One of the oldest playable organs in the world is in Sion.

56614.q: Which bid did the voters of Valais reject in 2018?
56614.e: In the vote, a majority said no to the funding for “Sion 2026”. That is why Switzerland withdrew the bid.
56614.m: In 2018 Valais said no to the Olympics in Sion.

56615.q: On which river does Sion lie?
56615.e: Sion lies in the middle of the Rhône valley in Valais. The Val d'Hérens also joins the Rhône valley near Sion.

56616.q: What is the northern part of Ticino above the Monte Ceneri called?
56616.e: “Sopra” means “above”. The southern part below the Ceneri is called the Sottoceneri.
56616.m: The Sopraceneri lies north of the Monte Ceneri.

56618.q: Which grape variety is grown most in Ticino?
56618.e: Merlot came to Ticino around 1906 and grows very well there. Today it makes up most of Ticino's vines.
56618.m: Merlot is the most important grape variety in Ticino.

56620.q: Which valley in Ticino leads up to the Lukmanier Pass?
56620.e: The Blenio Valley branches off at Biasca and leads north to the Lukmanier. Over the pass you reach Disentis in the Grisons.
56620.m: You travel through the Blenio Valley to the Lukmanier Pass.

56621.q: In which year was the Ceneri Base Tunnel opened?
56621.e: Since 2020 the 15-kilometre tunnel has connected the north and south of Ticino. It completed the New Rail Link through the Alps (NRLA).
56621.m: The Ceneri Base Tunnel has been in use since 2020.

56622.q: Which fruit used to be so important in Ticino that its tree was called the “bread tree”?
56622.e: Dried chestnuts and chestnut flour fed people in winter. Today chestnut festivals are held in autumn.
56622.m: The chestnut used to be the bread of the people of Ticino.

56623.q: What is the parliament of the canton of Ticino called?
56623.e: The Gran Consiglio (Grand Council) has 90 members and meets in Bellinzona. The Consiglio di Stato, on the other hand, is the government of Ticino.
56623.m: Ticino's parliament is called the Gran Consiglio.

56624.q: Bellinzona is the capital of which canton?
56624.e: Bellinzona is the capital of the canton of Ticino. The cantonal government and parliament meet there.
56624.m: Bellinzona is the capital of Ticino.

56625.q: What is Bellinzona's big carnival called?
56625.e: Rabadan is one of the biggest carnivals in Switzerland and takes place every year before Ash Wednesday. The other names belong to customs in Basel, Solothurn and Zurich.

56626.q: How many medieval castles are there in Bellinzona?
56626.e: Castelgrande, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro used to guard the route to the Alpine passes.

56627.q: What is Bellinzona's old town known for every Saturday morning?
56627.e: At the Saturday market traders sell vegetables, cheese, cured meats and crafts from Ticino. It attracts many visitors.
56627.m: There is a big market in Bellinzona every Saturday.

56628.q: Which of Bellinzona's castles is the biggest and stands on a rock in the middle of the town?
56628.e: Castelgrande towers on a rocky hill right above the old town. The name means big castle.
56628.m: Castelgrande is the biggest castle in Bellinzona.

56629.q: Which university based in Lugano was founded in 1996?
56629.e: The USI is the only university in Italian-speaking Switzerland. It has sites in Lugano, Mendrisio and Bellinzona.
56629.m: The university of Italian-speaking Switzerland is in Lugano.

56630.q: Lugano is the biggest city in which canton?
56630.e: Lugano is the biggest city in Ticino. But the capital of the canton is Bellinzona.
56630.m: Lugano is the biggest city in Ticino.

56631.q: Which country does the area around Lugano border just a few kilometres south of the city?
56631.e: Italy begins not far south of Lugano. Milan can be reached by train in about an hour.
56631.m: Lugano lies near the border with Italy.

56632.q: Why is landing at Lugano airport difficult for pilots?
a: It is surrounded by high mountains.
The runway is on a glacier.
It is in the middle of the lake.
56632.e: The small airport lies in a narrow valley near Agno. Because of the mountains all around, the approach is steep and needs specially trained pilots.
56632.m: Lugano airport lies squeezed between mountains.

56633.q: Which writer lived for over 40 years in Montagnola near Lugano?
56633.e: Hermann Hesse moved to Ticino in 1919 and wrote many books there. A museum in Montagnola remembers him.
56633.m: Hermann Hesse lived in Montagnola for a long time.

56634.q: What was agreed in Locarno in 1925?
a: Treaties to secure peace in Europe
The building of the Gotthard Tunnel
56634.e: At the Locarno Conference, Germany, France and other countries agreed on their borders in the west. The treaties were meant to secure peace after the First World War.
56634.m: In 1925 countries signed peace treaties in Locarno.

56636.q: Which flowers are shown in a well-known park on the lakeshore in Locarno?
56636.e: Over 1000 varieties of camellia grow in the Parco delle Camelie. They bloom in spring because the climate is so mild.
56636.m: Locarno is famous for its camellias.

56637.q: Which railway line connects Locarno with Domodossola in Italy?
56637.e: The narrow-gauge railway runs through the “valley of a hundred valleys” over many bridges. In Domodossola it connects with the Simplon line.
56637.m: The Centovalli Railway runs from Locarno to Domodossola.

56638.q: Which city is the second biggest in French-speaking Switzerland after Geneva?
56638.e: By population, Lausanne is in second place among the cities of western Switzerland, behind Geneva. It is the capital of the canton of Vaud.
56638.m: Lausanne is the second biggest city in French-speaking Switzerland.

56639.q: Which old language used to be spoken in most villages of French-speaking Switzerland?
56639.e: These dialects are also called patois. Today only a few older people still speak them, mainly in Valais.
56639.m: People in French-speaking Switzerland used to speak patois.

56640.q: What does the western Swiss word “panosse” mean?
56640.e: A “panosse” is a cloth for mopping the floor. In France people say “serpillière”.
56640.m: In French-speaking Switzerland you clean the floor with a “panosse”.

56641.q: What does the word “cornet” mean when shopping in French-speaking Switzerland?
56641.e: At the till in western Switzerland people ask: “Vous voulez un cornet?” They mean a plastic or paper bag.
56641.m: In French-speaking Switzerland a “cornet” is a shopping bag.

56642.q: What is the watchmaking region in the Jura arc between Geneva and Basel called?
56642.e: Many watch companies have their workshops in the Jura arc. The name is a reminder of Silicon Valley in California.
56642.m: The Jura arc is Switzerland's “Watch Valley”.

56643.q: Which canton was the first to give women the vote, in February 1959?
56643.e: Vaud was the first canton, followed shortly afterwards by Neuchâtel and, in 1960, by Geneva. At federal level women have only been allowed to vote since 1971.
56643.m: Vaud was the first canton to give women the vote.

56644.q: Why is the Röstigraben named after rösti?
a: Because it is seen as a typical German Swiss dish
Because it was invented in French-speaking Switzerland
Because it is only eaten in Valais
Because it is made from maize
56644.e: Rösti, made from grated potatoes, is seen as typical of German-speaking Switzerland. That is why it jokingly stands for the German-speaking side.

56645.q: What do people in French-speaking Switzerland often jokingly call the Röstigraben?
56645.e: “Rideau” means curtain. In western Switzerland people talk about the “rösti curtain” or the “barrière de rösti”.
56645.m: In French-speaking Switzerland the Röstigraben is called the “rideau de rösti”.

56646.q: In which well-known vote in 1992 did the Röstigraben show up especially clearly?
56646.e: French-speaking Switzerland clearly voted for joining the EEA, while most of German-speaking Switzerland voted against. Overall, joining was narrowly rejected.
56646.m: The 1992 EEA vote showed a deep Röstigraben.

56647.q: Which “divide” has often become more important than the Röstigraben in votes in recent years?
56647.e: More and more often, towns vote differently from rural municipalities. This difference is called the town-country divide.
56647.m: In votes the town-country divide often separates people more than the Röstigraben.

56648.q: In which war was there a deep divide because German-speaking Swiss tended to side with Germany and French-speaking Swiss with France?
56648.e: In the First World War the parts of the country argued fiercely. In 1914 the writer Carl Spitteler warned against this split in a speech.
56648.m: In the First World War the divide between the parts of the country was especially deep.

56649.q: Which two peoples settled on either side of the later language border in the early Middle Ages?
56649.e: The Burgundians took on the Romance language of the local population, while the Alemanni spoke a Germanic language. That is how the language border gradually came about.
56649.m: The language border goes back to the Alemanni and the Burgundians.

56650.q: Which Latin motto belongs to Geneva?
56650.e: “Post tenebras lux” means “After darkness, light”. The motto often appears above the Geneva coat of arms.

56651.q: What colour is the key on the Geneva coat of arms?
56651.e: The golden key stands upright on the red field. It is a reminder of the power of the bishops who used to rule Geneva.
56651.m: On the Geneva coat of arms there is a golden key on red.

56652.q: What colours is the coat of arms of Valais?
56652.e: The coat of arms is divided vertically, white on the left and red on the right. Stars in the opposite colours are spread across it.
56652.m: The Valais coat of arms is white and red.

56653.q: Which three colours does today's flag of the canton of Neuchâtel have?
56653.e: Since the revolution of 1848 Neuchâtel has had a green, white and red flag. At the top of the red field there is a small white cross.
56653.m: The Neuchâtel flag is green, white and red.

56654.q: What can you see above the Geneva coat of arms?
56654.e: A sun shines above the Geneva coat of arms. It goes with the motto “Post tenebras lux”, after darkness, light.
56654.m: A sun shines above the Geneva coat of arms.

56655.q: In how many cantons is German the only official language?
56655.e: German alone is official in 17 cantons. Bern, Fribourg and Valais are bilingual, the Grisons trilingual, and the remaining cantons are French- or Italian-speaking.
56655.m: German is the only official language in 17 cantons.

56656.q: What is the government called in most German-speaking cantons?
56656.e: In most cantons the cantonal government is called the Regierungsrat (government council). It usually has five or seven members.
56656.m: A canton is usually governed by the Regierungsrat.

56657.q: Which canton has the most municipalities?
56657.e: The canton of Bern has over 300 municipalities, more than any other canton (as of 2025).
56657.m: Bern is the canton with the most municipalities.

56658.q: Which abbreviation stands for the canton of Thurgau?
56658.e: Every canton has a two-letter abbreviation, which you see on number plates, for example. Thurgau's abbreviation is TG.
56658.m: The abbreviation for Thurgau is TG.

56659.q: Which cantons already existed at the time of the Federal Charter of 1291?
56659.e: The Federal Charter of 1291 was made by Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden. Only after that did other places gradually join.
56659.m: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden stood at the beginning of the Confederation.

56660.q: In politics, what else are the cantons called?
56660.e: The cantons are also called states (Stände). That is why the chamber in which they are represented is called the Council of States.
56660.m: The cantons are also called states.

56661.q: How many seats does the Council of States have in total?
56661.e: Each canton has two seats, the cantons with half a cantonal vote only one. Together that makes 46 seats.
56661.m: The Council of States has 46 members.

56662.q: How many half-cantons are there in Switzerland?
56662.e: The half-cantons are Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden. That makes six.
56662.m: There are six half-cantons in Switzerland.

56663.q: How many seats in the Council of States does a half-canton have?
56663.e: A half-canton sends only one person to the Council of States, a full canton sends two.
56663.m: Half-cantons have one seat each in the Council of States.

56664.q: How does a half-canton's vote count in the majority of the cantons?
56664.e: Changes to the constitution need a majority of the cantons. A half-canton counts only with half a vote.
56664.m: In the majority of the cantons a half-canton has half a cantonal vote.

56665.q: In which year was the canton of Basel split into Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft?
56665.e: After disputes and fighting between the city and the countryside, the canton of Basel was split in 1833. Since then there have been two Basel cantons.
56665.m: Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft have existed since 1833.

56666.q: How many cantonal votes are there in total in the majority of the cantons?
56666.e: 20 cantons have one whole vote each, plus the half cantonal votes, which together make 3 votes. 20 + 3 = 23.
56666.m: There are 23 cantonal votes in total in the majority of the cantons.

56667.q: Which half-canton still holds a Landsgemeinde every year?
56667.e: Nidwalden (1996), Ausserrhoden (1997) and Obwalden (1998) abolished their Landsgemeinde (open-air assembly). Apart from Innerrhoden, only the canton of Glarus still has a Landsgemeinde.
56667.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden is the only half-canton that still has a Landsgemeinde.

56668.q: Which canton has the most inhabitants after Zurich?
56668.e: About 1.06 million people live in the canton of Bern (as of the end of 2023). That puts it in second place.
56668.m: Bern is the canton with the second largest population.

56669.q: Which town is the biggest in the canton of Bern after Bern itself?
56669.e: At the end of 2023 Biel/Bienne had about 56,000 inhabitants. That makes it the second biggest town in the canton after the city of Bern, ahead of Thun.
56669.m: Biel/Bienne is the second biggest town in the canton of Bern.

56670.q: Which two official languages does the canton of Bern have?
56670.e: In the canton of Bern people mainly speak German, but in the Bernese Jura and in Biel they also speak French.
56670.m: The canton of Bern is bilingual, German and French.

56671.q: How many members does the cantonal government of Bern have?
56671.e: The Bernese government has seven members, who are elected by the people every four years.
56671.m: The Bernese cantonal government has seven members.

56672.q: In which holiday resort in the canton of Bern is an ATP Tour tennis tournament held every summer?
56672.e: The tournament in Gstaad is played on clay. The resort lies in the Saanenland at about 1050 metres above sea level.
56672.m: A big tennis tournament takes place in Gstaad every summer.

56673.q: What is the region in the south of the canton of Bern with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau called?
56673.e: The Bernese Oberland is the mountain region of the canton of Bern. Well-known places include Interlaken, Grindelwald and Lauterbrunnen.
56673.m: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau are in the Bernese Oberland.

56674.q: What is the parliament of the canton of Bern called?
56674.e: The Bernese cantonal parliament is called the Grand Council. It meets in the town hall in Bern's old town.
56674.m: The Bernese parliament is called the Grand Council.

56675.q: Which gorge near Meiringen can you walk through on walkways?
56675.e: Between Meiringen and Innertkirchen the Aare has cut deep into a ridge of limestone. You can cross the narrow Aare Gorge on walkways.
56675.m: The Aare Gorge is near Meiringen in the Bernese Oberland.

56676.q: Which canton in Central Switzerland has the most inhabitants?
56676.e: Over 400,000 people live in the canton of Lucerne, more than in any other canton of Central Switzerland.
56676.m: Lucerne is the most populous canton in Central Switzerland.

56677.q: Which small town in Lucerne is known for a ring-shaped biscuit?
56677.e: The hard, sweet Willisauer Ringli have been made in Willisau since the 19th century.

56678.q: Lucerne was the first city to join the Swiss Confederation. In which year?
56678.e: In 1332 Lucerne formed an alliance with Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden. It was the first town in the alliance.
56678.m: Lucerne joined the Confederation in 1332 as the first city.

56679.q: What colours is the coat of arms of the canton of Lucerne?
56679.e: The Lucerne coat of arms is divided vertically into a blue half and a white half.
56679.m: The Lucerne coat of arms is blue and white, divided vertically.

56680.q: What goes bang at 5 o'clock in the morning on “Dirty Thursday” to start the Lucerne carnival?
56680.e: At the early morning wake-up, Brother Fritschi arrives in the city by boat. A loud bang, the Urknall (“Big Bang”), is then the starting signal for the Guggenmusig bands.
56680.m: The Lucerne carnival begins with the Urknall.

56681.q: On which lake is the Swiss Ornithological Institute?
56681.e: The Swiss Ornithological Institute studies birds and is based in Sempach on Lake Sempach.
56681.m: The Ornithological Institute is in Sempach on Lake Sempach.

56683.q: What else were Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden called in the Middle Ages?
56683.e: The three valley communities by the lake were called the forest cantons, or Waldstätte. That is also where the German name of Lake Lucerne, Vierwaldstättersee, comes from.
56683.m: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden used to be called the forest cantons.

56684.q: According to legend, on which meadow by Lake Uri was the oath of the Confederates sworn?
56684.e: According to legend, representatives of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swore the oath of alliance on the Rütli. The meadow is in the canton of Uri.
56684.m: The Rütli is seen as the place of the legendary oath.

56685.q: According to legend, where did William Tell shoot the bailiff Gessler?
a: In the Hohle Gasse near Küssnacht
56685.e: According to legend, Tell lay in wait for the bailiff in the Hohle Gasse (sunken lane) near Küssnacht in the canton of Schwyz.
56685.m: The Hohle Gasse near Küssnacht is part of the Tell legend.

56686.q: Which poet wrote the play “William Tell” in 1804?
56686.e: Friedrich Schiller made the Tell legend famous all over the world with his drama of 1804, although he himself never went to Switzerland.
56686.m: Friedrich Schiller wrote the drama “William Tell”.

56687.q: In which valley in Schwyz do the “weather sniffers” forecast the weather?
56687.e: The weather sniffers (Wetterschmöcker) of the Muotatal watch nature and animals and use them to make their weather forecasts twice a year.
56687.m: The weather sniffers come from the Muotatal.

56688.q: Which village in the canton of Schwyz was buried by a big landslide in 1806?
56688.e: On 2 September 1806 huge masses of rock fell from the Rossberg onto Goldau. About 450 people died.
56688.m: Goldau was destroyed by a landslide in 1806.

56689.q: Which holiday is a reminder of the Federal Charter of early August 1291?
a: The Day of Prayer in September
56689.e: Because the Federal Charter is dated early August 1291, Switzerland celebrates its national holiday on 1 August.
56689.m: 1 August is a reminder of the Federal Charter of 1291.

56690.q: Which municipality in the canton of Zug has the most inhabitants after the town of Zug?
56690.e: Baar lies directly north of Zug and, with over 20,000 inhabitants, is the second biggest municipality in Zug.
56690.m: Baar is the second biggest municipality in the canton of Zug.

56692.q: Which mountain above the town of Zug can be reached by funicular?
56692.e: The Zugerberg funicular runs from Zug up the Zugerberg, which is about 1000 metres high.
56692.m: A funicular goes up the Zugerberg.

56693.q: What is the canton of Zug especially known for in business?
a: Low taxes and many company headquarters
56693.e: Zug has very low taxes. That is why many international companies have their headquarters there.
56693.m: Zug is known for low taxes and many company headquarters.

56694.q: What is the Zug custom called in which people race with ladders to cherry trees?
56694.e: The Chriesisturm (cherry storm) is a reminder of the old days when the cherry harvest was officially opened. Today teams run through the town of Zug with ladders.
56694.m: The Chriesisturm is a cherry custom from Zug.

56695.q: What nickname does the Zug region have because of the many companies in the blockchain industry?
56695.e: Because many companies dealing with cryptocurrencies have settled in Zug, the region is called Crypto Valley.
56695.m: Zug is also called Crypto Valley.

56696.q: What are the two nuclear power stations in the canton of Aargau called?
56696.e: Beznau and Leibstadt are both in Aargau. Gösgen is in the canton of Solothurn, Mühleberg in the canton of Bern.
56696.m: Beznau and Leibstadt are the nuclear power stations in Aargau.

56697.q: Where does Aargau rank among the cantons by number of inhabitants?
56697.e: Only Zurich, Bern and Vaud have more inhabitants than Aargau.
56697.m: Aargau is the fourth biggest canton by population.

56698.q: Which region of Aargau belonged to Austria until 1802?
56698.e: The Fricktal belonged to the Habsburgs for a long time and only came to Switzerland in 1802, shortly before the canton of Aargau was created.
56698.m: The Fricktal belonged to Austria until 1802.

56699.q: Which monastery in the Freiamt did the Habsburgs found in 1027?
56699.e: The Benedictine abbey of Muri was founded in 1027 by ancestors of the Habsburgs and was their family monastery for a long time.
56699.m: Muri Abbey was founded by the Habsburgs.

56700.q: In which town in Aargau did the Diet of the old Confederation meet especially often?
56700.e: From the 15th to the 18th century the envoys of the Confederate states often met in Baden town hall.
56700.m: The Diet often met in Baden.

56701.q: What is special about Hallwyl Castle in Aargau?
a: It stands on islands in the water
It is made entirely of glass
56701.e: Hallwyl Castle is a moated castle. It stands on two islands in the Aabach stream near Lake Hallwil.
56701.m: Hallwyl Castle is a moated castle.

56703.q: Which castle towers on a hill above the Aargau town of the same name and is now a museum?
56703.e: Lenzburg Castle is one of the oldest and biggest castles in Switzerland and houses a museum.
56703.m: Lenzburg Castle towers above the town of Lenzburg.

56704.q: Since which year have the Grisons been a canton of Switzerland?
56704.e: For a long time the Grisons were an associated territory. With the Act of Mediation they became a full canton in 1803.
56704.m: The Grisons have been a Swiss canton since 1803.

56705.q: Where does the canton of the Grisons (Graubünden in German) get its name from?
a: From the fog in the Rhine valley
56705.e: The Grisons grew out of the Three Leagues: the League of God's House, the League of the Ten Jurisdictions and the Grey League.
56705.m: The Grisons are named after the Grey League.

56706.q: Which three official languages do the Grisons have?
56706.e: The Grisons are the only trilingual canton. The official languages are German, Romansh and Italian.
56706.m: The Grisons are the only trilingual canton.

56707.q: Which monastery in the Val Müstair is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
56707.e: The Convent of St John in Müstair is famous for its wall paintings from the time of Charlemagne. It has been a World Heritage Site since 1983.
56707.m: The Convent of St John in Müstair is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

56708.q: Which municipality in the Grisons is the biggest in Switzerland by area?
56708.e: Since several municipalities merged in 2015, Scuol in the Lower Engadine has been the biggest municipality in Switzerland, at about 439 square kilometres.
56708.m: Scuol is the biggest municipality in Switzerland by area.

56709.q: Which lines of the Rhaetian Railway have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008?
56709.e: The Albula and Bernina lines, with the Landwasser Viaduct and many spiral tunnels, have been a World Heritage Site since 2008.
56709.m: The Albula and Bernina lines are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

56710.q: Which Benedictine monastery lies on the Vorderrhein in the Surselva?
56710.e: Disentis Abbey was founded in the 8th century and still shapes the village on the Vorderrhein today.
56710.m: Disentis Abbey lies in the Surselva.

56711.q: What nickname do the Grisons have because of their many valleys?
56711.e: The Grisons are criss-crossed by countless main valleys and side valleys. That is why they are called the “land of 150 valleys”.
56711.m: The Grisons are also called the land of 150 valleys.

56712.q: Which canton completely surrounds the two Appenzells?
56712.e: Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Innerrhoden lie like an island in the middle of the canton of St Gallen.
56712.m: The two Appenzells are completely surrounded by St Gallen.

56713.q: What do men traditionally carry at the Landsgemeinde in Appenzell to show they can vote?
56713.e: Traditionally the sword or side arm shows that a man is entitled to vote. Women and others show a voting card.
56713.m: The sword is a traditional proof of the right to vote at the Landsgemeinde.

56715.q: In which year did women in Appenzell Innerrhoden get the right to vote at cantonal level?
56715.e: As the last canton, Innerrhoden had to introduce votes for women in 1990, after the Federal Supreme Court ruled that it must.
56715.m: In 1990 Appenzell Innerrhoden became the last canton to give women the vote.

56716.q: Which is the highest mountain in the Alpstein?
56716.e: The Säntis is about 2500 metres high and the highest peak in the Alpstein. There is a big transmitter mast on its summit.
56716.m: The Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein.

56717.q: Into how many cantons is the Appenzell region divided?
56717.e: Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden have existed since 1597. The split had to do with the Reformation.
56717.m: The Appenzell region consists of two cantons.

56718.q: Which breed of dog comes from the Appenzell region?
56718.e: The Appenzeller Sennenhund is a medium-sized, three-coloured herding dog. In the past it helped to drive cattle and guard farms.
56718.m: The Appenzeller Sennenhund comes from the Appenzell region.

56719.q: What is the parliament of the canton of St Gallen called?
56719.e: The St Gallen parliament is called the Cantonal Council (Kantonsrat) and meets in the government building in the Abbey District.
56719.m: The St Gallen parliament is called the Cantonal Council.

56720.q: Which spa resort in St Gallen uses warm spring water from the Tamina Gorge?
56720.e: The thermal water comes from the Tamina Gorge near Pfäfers and is piped to Bad Ragaz.
56720.m: Bad Ragaz is a spa resort with thermal water.

56721.q: Which port town in St Gallen lies on Lake Constance?
56721.e: Rorschach lies on the southern shore of Lake Constance and has a harbour for passenger boats.
56721.m: Rorschach is the St Gallen port town on Lake Constance.

56722.q: Which town in St Gallen is called the “town of the abbots”?
56722.e: For a long time Wil was the residence of the prince-abbots of St Gallen. That is why the town is called the town of the abbots.
56722.m: Wil is called the town of the abbots.

56723.q: What is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of St Gallen?
a: A bundle of rods with an axe
56723.e: The St Gallen coat of arms shows a bundle of rods with an axe, a symbol of unity.
56723.m: The St Gallen coat of arms shows a bundle of rods.

56724.q: Which two countries does the canton of St Gallen border in the Rhine valley?
56724.e: In the St Gallen Rhine valley the Rhine forms the border with Austria and with Liechtenstein.
56724.m: St Gallen borders Austria and Liechtenstein.

56725.q: Which ski and hiking area in the canton of St Gallen lies high above Lake Walen?
56725.e: Flumserberg lies above Flums. From there you can see Lake Walen and the Churfirsten.

56726.q: In which year was the canton of St Gallen founded?
56726.e: The canton of St Gallen was created in 1803 by Napoleon's Act of Mediation. It was formed from former lands of the prince-abbot and several subject territories.
56726.m: The canton of St Gallen was created in 1803.

56727.q: In which two places does the Thurgau Grand Council meet in turn?
56727.e: In the summer half of the year the Grand Council meets in Frauenfeld, in the winter half in Weinfelden.
56727.m: The Thurgau Grand Council meets in Frauenfeld and in Weinfelden.

56729.q: Which later French emperor grew up at Arenenberg Castle in Thurgau?
56729.e: Louis-Napoléon spent his youth at Arenenberg with his mother Hortense. Today the Napoleon Museum is there.
56729.m: Napoleon III grew up at Arenenberg.

56730.e: From 1460 Thurgau was a common lordship. The Confederate states took turns to appoint a bailiff.
56730.m: Until 1798 Thurgau was a common lordship of the Confederates.

56731.q: What is the range of hills between the Thur valley and the Untersee called?
56731.e: The Seerücken runs from west to east through the north of Thurgau, parallel to the Untersee.
56731.m: The Seerücken lies between the Thur valley and the Untersee.

56732.q: Which small town in Thurgau is connected to Germany by a covered wooden bridge over the Rhine?
56732.e: The wooden bridge from 1816 connects Diessenhofen with the German village of Gailingen. There the Rhine forms the national border.
56732.m: At Diessenhofen an old wooden bridge leads to Germany.

56733.q: In which year did Thurgau become a canton in its own right?
56733.e: Before that, Thurgau was a subject territory of the Confederates. In 1803 it became a canton with equal rights through the Act of Mediation.
56733.m: Thurgau has been a canton in its own right since 1803.

56734.q: How many separate parts does the canton of Schaffhausen consist of?
56734.e: The canton has one big main part and two smaller areas, one around Stein am Rhein and one around Rüdlingen and Buchberg.
56734.m: The canton of Schaffhausen consists of three separate parts.

56735.q: Which two cantons does the canton of Schaffhausen border?
56735.e: Apart from Germany, Schaffhausen only borders the cantons of Zurich and Thurgau.

56736.q: What is the round fortress towering above the town of Schaffhausen called?
56736.e: The Munot is a round fortress from the 16th century and the landmark of the town of Schaffhausen.
56736.m: The Munot is the landmark of Schaffhausen.

56737.q: In which year did Schaffhausen join the Swiss Confederation?
56737.e: Schaffhausen became a member of the Confederation in 1501, in the same year as Basel.

56738.q: What is the former monastery in Schaffhausen that is now a big museum called?
56738.e: All Saints Abbey (Allerheiligen) was founded in the 11th century. Today the Museum zu Allerheiligen shows history, art and nature.
56738.m: The Museum zu Allerheiligen is a former monastery.

56739.q: What happened in the town of Schaffhausen on 1 April 1944?
a: It was destroyed by an earthquake
56739.e: American planes bombed Schaffhausen by mistake because they thought they were over Germany. About 40 people died.
56739.m: Schaffhausen was bombed by mistake in 1944.

56740.q: Which small town in the canton of Schaffhausen is known for its painted house fronts?
56740.e: The old town of Stein am Rhein is famous for its half-timbered houses and beautifully painted facades.
56740.m: Stein am Rhein is known for painted facades.

56741.q: How many municipalities belong to the canton of Basel-Stadt?
56741.e: The canton is made up of the city of Basel and the two rural municipalities of Riehen and Bettingen.

56742.q: Which stone is Basel Minster built from?
56742.e: The minster above the Rhine is built from red sandstone. That is why it glows reddish.
56742.m: Basel Minster is made of red sandstone.

56743.q: Above which river does Basel Minster stand?
56743.e: The minster stands on a hill high above the Rhine. From the Pfalz terrace behind the church you can see far across the river.
56743.m: Basel Minster stands above the Rhine.

56744.q: Which Basel custom has been part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage since 2017?
56744.e: Basel Carnival, with the Morgestraich, the Cliques, piccolos and drums, was recognised by UNESCO in 2017.
56744.m: Basel Carnival is UNESCO intangible cultural heritage.

56745.q: Which artist created the Carnival Fountain with moving figures by the Basel theatre?
56745.e: The Tinguely Fountain is made of machines that spray water. There is also a Tinguely Museum in Basel.
56745.m: Jean Tinguely created the Carnival Fountain in Basel.

56746.q: Which region moved from the canton of Bern to the canton of Basel-Landschaft in 1994?
56746.e: After a popular vote, the Laufental moved from the canton of Bern to Basel-Landschaft on 1 January 1994.
56746.m: The Laufental has belonged to Basel-Landschaft since 1994.

56748.q: How did the two Basels vote on a merger in 2014?
56748.e: In September 2014 Basel-Stadt voted to look into a merger, but Basel-Landschaft clearly rejected it. The cantons stayed separate.
56748.m: In 2014 Basel-Landschaft rejected a merger with Basel-Stadt.

56749.q: Which major region of Switzerland lies in the north-west of the country?
56749.e: The Jura stretches in an arc from the Geneva area to the region around Schaffhausen. It forms the north-west of Switzerland on the border with France.
56749.m: The Jura is the major region in the north-west of Switzerland.

56750.q: Which industry is traditionally especially strong in the Swiss Jura?
56750.e: Watchmaking developed from the 18th century in places such as La Chaux-de-Fonds, Le Locle and the Vallée de Joux. It is still an important employer in the Jura arc today.
56750.m: The Jura is the home of the Swiss watch industry.

56751.q: How do the mountains of the Jura differ from the Alps?
a: They are higher and more pointed
56751.e: The Jura mountains are at most about 1700 metres high and have rounded, wooded ridges. The Alps are much higher and have glaciers.
56751.m: The Jura is lower and gentler than the Alps.

56752.q: Which period of Earth's history is named after the Jura Mountains?
56752.e: The rocks from this time were studied especially well in the Jura Mountains. That is why the period from about 200 to 145 million years ago is called the “Jurassic”.
56752.m: The Jurassic period is named after the Jura Mountains.

56753.q: Between which two lakes does the Swiss Plateau stretch?
56753.e: The Swiss Plateau reaches from Lake Geneva in the south-west to Lake Constance in the north-east. It lies between the Jura and the Alps.
56753.m: The Swiss Plateau reaches from Lake Geneva to Lake Constance.

56754.q: At what height does the Swiss Plateau lie on average?
56754.e: The Swiss Plateau is a hilly plain that mostly lies between 400 and 600 metres above sea level. Some hills rise much higher.
56754.m: The Swiss Plateau mostly lies at 400 to 600 metres above sea level.

56755.q: What is the rock made of sand, marl and gravel that forms the ground beneath the Swiss Plateau called?
56755.e: Molasse formed from the debris that rivers carried from the young Alps into a basin in front of them. Sandstone, marl and conglomerate are part of it.
56755.m: The ground beneath the Swiss Plateau is made of molasse.

56756.q: Roughly how long is the Swiss Plateau from Lake Geneva to Lake Constance?
56756.e: On Swiss territory the Swiss Plateau stretches for about 300 km. It is narrow in the south-west and gets wider towards the north-east.
56756.m: The Swiss Plateau is about 300 kilometres long.

56757.q: Which two big rivers flow through long valleys right through the Swiss Alps, one to the west and the other to the east?
56757.e: The Rhône flows west through Valais, the Rhine east through the Grisons. Together their valleys form a long furrow through the Alps.
56757.m: The Rhône and the Rhine flow in long valleys across the Alps.

56758.q: Roughly how many four-thousanders are on Swiss territory?
56758.e: On Swiss territory there are 48 peaks over 4000 metres above sea level. Most of them are in Valais.

56759.q: What is the line of the highest peaks that divides the Alps into a northern and a southern side called?
56759.e: The main Alpine ridge is the main watershed of the Alps. North of it is the northern side of the Alps, south of it the southern side.
56759.m: The main Alpine ridge divides the Alps into north and south.

56760.q: Which rocks are the central massifs of the Swiss Alps, such as the Aar Massif, mainly made of?
56760.e: The central massifs are made of very old crystalline rock. Granite and gneiss are hard and form many high, steep peaks.
56760.m: The central massifs of the Alps are mainly made of granite and gneiss.

56761.q: How was the Folded Jura formed?
56761.e: The pressure from the formation of the Alps pushed the limestone layers of the Jura together. This created parallel ridges and valleys, like a tablecloth pushed together.
56761.m: In the Folded Jura rock layers were folded into ridges.

56762.q: What is a narrow cross valley called, where a river cuts through a Jura ridge?
56762.e: A Klus (cluse) is a gorge cutting across a Jura ridge. A well-known example is the Klus of Balsthal.
56762.m: A Klus is a narrow gorge cutting through a Jura ridge.

56763.q: How do the mountain ridges of the Folded Jura run?
a: In a circle around a peak
56763.e: The folded rock layers form long ridges that run side by side from south-west to north-east. Between them lie long valleys.
56763.m: In the Folded Jura long, parallel ridges line up.

56764.q: Which mountain, at about 1600 metres above sea level, is the highest peak of the Bernese Jura?
56764.e: The Chasseral reaches 1607 metres above sea level and lies between Lake Biel and the Vallon de Saint-Imier.
56764.m: The Chasseral is the highest mountain in the Bernese Jura.

56765.q: Which valley in the Neuchâtel Jura is seen as the home of absinthe?
56765.e: The herbal spirit absinthe was first made in the Val de Travers at the end of the 18th century. The valley lies between two Jura ridges.
56765.m: The Val de Travers is the home of absinthe.

56766.q: How do the rock layers lie in the Tabular Jura?
56766.e: In the Tabular Jura the layers were hardly folded and lie almost flat like a table top. Rivers have cut valleys into these plates.
56766.m: In the Tabular Jura the rock layers lie almost horizontally.

56767.q: Which region in the canton of Aargau belongs to the Tabular Jura?
56767.e: The Fricktal lies north of the Jura ridge between the Aare and the Rhine. Its plateaus and valleys belong to the Tabular Jura.
56767.m: The Fricktal in Aargau lies in the Tabular Jura.

56768.q: In which part of the Swiss Jura is the Tabular Jura?
a: In the south on Lake Geneva
56768.e: In the north-east the rock layers of the Jura lie almost flat, so it is called the Tabular Jura. In the south-west, on the other hand, the Folded Jura dominates.
56768.m: The Tabular Jura lies in the north-east of the Swiss Jura.

56769.q: Which canton lies largely in the Tabular Jura?
56769.e: A good part of Basel-Landschaft is Tabular Jura with plateaus and deeply cut valleys. Only its south belongs to the Folded Jura.
56769.m: Basel-Landschaft lies largely in the Tabular Jura.

56770.q: Which Prealpine mountain between Lake Lucerne and Lake Zug is called the “Queen of the Mountains”?
56770.e: The Rigi is about 1800 m high and almost completely surrounded by lakes. Its cog railway from Vitznau is the oldest mountain railway in Europe.
56770.m: The Rigi is called the Queen of the Mountains.

56771.q: Which mountain on Lake Lucerne is a well-known peak of the Central Swiss Prealps?
56771.e: Pilatus above Lucerne is 2128 m high and belongs to the Central Swiss Prealps. It is a popular mountain for day trips.
56771.m: Pilatus is a Prealpine mountain above Lucerne.

56772.q: Which mountain in the Alpstein, at about 2500 m, is the highest peak of the eastern Swiss Prealps?
56772.e: The Säntis is 2502 metres above sea level and rises on the border of the two Appenzells and St Gallen.
56772.m: The Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein.

56773.q: Which peak of the Bernese Prealps can be reached by cable car from Erlenbach in the Simmental?
56773.e: The Stockhorn is about 2190 m high and lies west of Thun. It belongs to the Bernese Prealps and is a popular viewpoint mountain.
56773.m: The Stockhorn is a viewpoint mountain in the Bernese Prealps.

56774.q: Which use of the land is especially typical of the Prealps?
56774.e: In the Prealps many cows are taken up to alpine pastures in summer. Alpine cheese and other products are made from their milk.
56774.m: Alpine farming plays a big role in the Prealps.

56776.q: Which nature area south of Bern belongs to the Bernese Prealps?
56776.e: The Gantrisch area lies between Bern, Thun and Fribourg. It has been recognised as a nature park and belongs to the Prealps.
56776.m: The Gantrisch area lies in the Bernese Prealps.

56777.q: Why are the Prealps less high and rugged than the High Alps?
a: They lie on the edge of the mountain range
They are much younger than the Jura
They are made of volcanic rock
56777.e: The Prealps form the outer edge of the Alps. There the sheets of rock are not stacked so high, so the mountains are usually lower and rounder.
56777.m: The Prealps are the lower outer edge of the Alps.

56778.q: Which eerie story by Jeremias Gotthelf takes place in the Emmental?
a: The Rider on the White Horse
56778.e: Gotthelf published “The Black Spider” in 1842. The story takes place in the area around Sumiswald in the Emmental.
56778.m: Gotthelf's “The Black Spider” takes place in the Emmental.

56779.q: Which type of settlement is typical of the Emmental?
56779.e: In the hilly Emmental many farms stand on their own on the slopes and ridges. There are fewer big, compact villages there.
56779.m: In the Emmental many farms stand scattered on their own.

56780.q: What job did the writer Jeremias Gotthelf have in the Emmental?
56780.e: Jeremias Gotthelf's real name was Albert Bitzius, and he was the pastor in Lützelflüh. Alongside this he wrote many novels about life in the Emmental.
56780.m: Jeremias Gotthelf was a pastor in the Emmental.

56781.q: Which town is seen as the “gateway to the Emmental”?
56781.e: Burgdorf lies where the Emmental opens onto the Swiss Plateau. Burgdorf Castle towers above the old town.
56781.m: Burgdorf is seen as the gateway to the Emmental.

56782.q: Which farmer from the Emmental led the Bernese farmers in the Swiss Peasants' War of 1653?
56782.e: Niklaus Leuenberger came from Rüderswil in the Emmental. He was the leader of the farmers' league that rose up against the authorities in 1653.
56782.m: Niklaus Leuenberger led the Emmental farmers in the Peasants' War of 1653.

56783.e: The Emmental is a very varied hilly country. Narrow ravines alternate with ridges, known locally as “Eggen”.
56783.m: The Emmental is hilly country with ravines and ridges.

56784.q: Which place is the biggest in the upper Emmental?
56784.e: Langnau is the regional centre of the upper Emmental. There are schools, shops and an important railway station there.
56784.m: Langnau is the centre of the upper Emmental.

56785.q: Which typical Swiss team sport is played especially often in the Emmental?
56785.e: In Hornussen the Nouss, a small plastic puck, is hit far into the field. The other team tries to stop it with flat wooden boards.
56785.m: Hornussen is a popular sport in the Emmental.

56786.q: Roughly how high is the Napf?
56786.e: The Napf reaches about 1400 metres above sea level. It is the highest peak of the Napf hill country between the Emmental and the Entlebuch.
56786.m: The Napf is about 1400 metres high.

56787.q: On the border of which two cantons is the Napf?
56787.e: The summit with the mountain inn is on Bernese soil, and the canton of Lucerne begins just north of it.
56787.m: The Napf lies on the border of Bern and Lucerne.

56788.q: Which rock is the Napf mainly made of?
56788.e: The Napf is built of Nagelfluh, a conglomerate. This rock is made of rounded pebbles that rivers carried here from the Alps.
56788.m: The Napf is mainly made of Nagelfluh.

56789.q: Which well-known Bernese landscape lies at the foot of the Napf?
56789.e: The Napf rises between the Emmental in the canton of Bern and the Entlebuch in the canton of Lucerne.
56789.m: The Napf lies between the Emmental and the Entlebuch.

56790.q: What does the Napf hill country typically look like?
a: Ridges spreading out like a star with deep ravines
56790.e: Many narrow ridges run from the Napf in all directions like rays. Between them, streams have cut deep, steep ravines.
